transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for having me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time—it's probably not a huge deal, but... I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I've been having a little trouble just, well, staying in my chair? 

Like, I keep getting up during things where I know I really should stay put. Um, for example, during our sprint planning meetings at work, or recently I was on some really important mortgage calls. I'll just suddenly feel like I absolutely need to go get a glass of water right that second, or I'll decide I have to go check something in the other room. 

I'm really not trying to be rude or unprofessional, I promise! It's just a weird habit I can't quite seem to shake. Is... is that the kind of thing that makes sense to come in for? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Can you tell me when you first started noticing this restlessness and need to get up—was this something you experienced as a child, or did it start more recently as an adult?

Um, well, I guess it's not entirely new? I mean, I've always been a little... energetic, I suppose. 

Even back in elementary school, I remember my teachers sometimes having to, um, move my desk around. Or they'd gently remind me to stay in my seat because I had this habit of just popping up out of nowhere. And I guess I also had a tendency to talk before being called on, or I'd rush through my assignments, even though I actually understood the work perfectly fine. 

I was just eager, you know? I really wasn't trying to be a bad kid or anything—I just had a lot of enthusiasm. Does that make sense? I hope that answers your question.
Aside from the restlessness, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks, lose track of details, or forget things like appointments or where you put items?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I'm terribly forgetful or anything like that. I'm usually pretty good about my appointments and keeping track of my things, I think. But, um, as for staying focused... I guess maybe a little? 

Like, I can sit down to review a pull request for work, or, you know, when I was reading through those mortgage documents recently, I'll start out with really good intentions. I want to be thorough. But then, after a few minutes, I'll kind of realize I've been staring at the exact same section and my mind has just wandered off to, like, five completely unrelated things. 

It's not that I don't care about the work, I promise! I just get a little sidetracked sometimes. I usually catch myself, though. Is... is that normal? I mean, everyone's mind wanders a little bit, right? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Do you often make careless mistakes in your work or have trouble organizing tasks and keeping things in order, even when you're trying your best to focus?

Um, careless mistakes? No, no, I don't think so. I really try to be careful with my code, and I'm pretty diligent about double-checking things. I wouldn't want anyone to think I don't take my job seriously! 

But, um... organization? I guess maybe I struggle a tiny bit there? It's just that I have so many different things going on, you know? Like, I'll have work tickets, and then notes about fixing things around the house, and reminders for the budget... and I sort of just put them wherever is easiest at the time. So some things are in Slack, some are on sticky notes, some are in my email, or just on my phone. 

I mean, I always get things done eventually! It just... well, sometimes I think I might spend a little more time trying to figure out where I wrote down what I was supposed to do than actually, you know, doing it. But I'm sure lots of people have messy systems, right? It's not a huge problem, I just need to find a better app or something. Does that sound like what you were asking about?

Have you ever had ongoing problems with things like frequently arguing with authority figures, breaking rules, being aggressive, or getting into serious trouble at school or work because of behavior issues, either as a child or now?

Oh, goodness, no. No, definitely not. I've never been one to argue or cause trouble. I really respect rules and the people in charge, you know? 

Even back in school, like I mentioned, I might have been a little squirmy or talked out of turn sometimes, but I was always very respectful to my teachers. I always wanted them to like me! And at work, I have a great relationship with my managers. I would never want to be seen as difficult or aggressive. That's just... that's really not who I am at all. 

I've always tried my best to be cooperative and do what's expected of me. I hope that's clear? I really wouldn't want you to think I'm a rebellious person or anything like that.
Do you often find it hard to listen closely when people are talking directly to you, or do you frequently lose things you need, like keys, your phone, or paperwork?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really try to be a good listener. When someone is talking to me, especially at work or, you know, my husband, I make a real effort to pay attention. I mean, maybe sometimes if I'm really caught up in a coding problem, I might need them to repeat something, but I think that's pretty normal when you're concentrating hard, right? I certainly don't ignore people on purpose. 

And as for losing things... no, I'm usually pretty careful. I have a little bowl by the door for my keys, and my phone is almost always in my pocket or on my desk. I might misplace a pen now and then, but nothing important like paperwork or my wallet. I try to keep things where they belong so I don't cause any unnecessary stress. I'm doing okay with that part, aren't I?
Do you often find yourself blurting out answers or interrupting others before they've finished speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Oh, I really try not to be rude! I know how frustrating it is when people interrupt, and I definitely don't want to be *that* person. I always try to be polite and wait my turn. 

But, um... I guess maybe at work, I do get a little ahead of myself sometimes? Just a little. Like, if a teammate is explaining a bug to me, or asking a question... I sometimes catch myself answering them before they’ve actually finished. I just get so eager to help solve it, you know? But then... well, sometimes I’m already talking and I realize I completely guessed wrong about where they were going with the question. 

I always apologize right away, though! I really just want to be helpful and fix the problem quickly for them. I think it's mostly just me being a little too enthusiastic, right? I really hope my coworkers don't think I'm being disrespectful. Does that sound like a bad thing to you?
Do you notice these same patterns—like restlessness, interrupting, or losing focus—happening at home or in your personal relationships, not just at work?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I really try to keep everything running smoothly at home, I promise I do. I want my husband to feel supported, and I want my coworkers to know they can count on me. I'm always trying my best.

But lately, I suppose... well, I've noticed people having to check in with me a bit more often than they used to. Like, my husband might have to remind me about a dinner plan, or a teammate will ask if I've finished that code review I said I'd do. It's nothing huge! Just... little things. 

It does create a tiny bit of friction sometimes, which I feel terrible about. I really hate the idea that I might be becoming the unreliable one when it comes to planning things or following through, especially because I'm trying so hard to stay on top of it all. I just want everyone to be happy with me, you know? I'm not doing a terrible job, am I? I just get a little scattered sometimes.

You mentioned your husband and coworkers have had to check in with you more often lately—has this pattern of needing reminders and follow-up been going on for at least six months, or is it something more recent?

Oh, um, well... I wouldn't say it's a completely new thing, no. I mean, I've always been a little energetic, but... I guess it's been noticeably harder to keep track of everything for maybe... about two years now? 

I really think it just started when we bought our house. Taking on the mortgage, and all the extra paperwork, and the planning, and just the mental load of it all... it was a lot, you know? I really tried to handle it all perfectly so my husband wouldn't have to worry, but I think that's when the little slip-ups started happening more often. 

It's just because I took on too much at once, right? I mean, anyone would get a little overwhelmed and need a reminder or two with all that extra responsibility, don't you think? I'm sure it's completely normal to struggle a bit when life gets that busy. I really am trying my best to stay organized.
